q.t: Adolescence is roughly between which ages?
q.e: Adolescence starts around 10–12 and lasts to about 19 — the stage between childhood and adulthood.

q.t: The stage when the body changes to become capable of reproduction is called…
q.e: Puberty is the set of body changes that prepare it for adulthood and reproduction.

q.t: The voice box is also called the…
q.e: The larynx is the voice box. It grows during puberty, changing the voice.

q.t: The bump in a boy's throat caused by a larger voice box is called the…
q.e: When the larynx grows larger in boys it can show as a visible bump — the Adam's apple.

q.t: Pimples during adolescence are caused by…
q.e: More oil is made by skin glands; clogged pores get infected and show as pimples. The condition is called acne.

q.t: The menstrual cycle usually repeats about every…
q.e: About 28–30 days is typical, though 21–35 days is also common and healthy.

q.t: Which nutrient helps in the formation of blood?
q.e: Iron is needed to make blood. Spinach, kidney beans, raisins and figs are good sources.

q.t: Milk, curd and paneer are important for…
q.e: They provide calcium and protein, which build strong bones.

q.t: Using phones or the internet to harass someone is called…
q.e: Cyberbullying includes spreading rumours, misleading messages or sharing someone's personal information without consent.

q.t: If you are cyberbullied, what should you do?
o: Delete all your photos and stay quiet
q.e: Don't feel scared or helpless — trusted adults can help you handle it.

q.t: Voice change, facial hair in boys and breast development in girls are called…
q.e: They tell males and females apart but are not themselves part of reproduction — they signal that puberty has started.

q.t: Why does the voice change more in boys than in girls?
o: The larynx grows larger in boys
q.e: The larynx grows in both, but more in boys, giving a deeper voice.

q.t: Two classmates of the same age are very different in height. This is…
q.e: The timing and amount of change varies from person to person. Every variation is normal.

q.t: Menstruation usually lasts…
q.e: The bleeding phase usually lasts 3–7 days within the roughly month-long cycle.

q.t: Menstruation stops naturally at about what age?
q.e: Menstrual cycles stop naturally around 45–55 years.

q.t: Which vitamin cannot be made by our body and must come from food?
q.e: B12 must come from the diet; lack of it (or iron) can cause anaemia.

q.t: How should used sanitary pads be disposed of?
o: Wrapped in newspaper, in a dustbin
q.e: Wrapping and binning keeps the surroundings clean and protects community health.

q.t: Why are substances like tobacco and alcohol especially harmful?
o: They are addictive and damage body and mind
q.e: They harm physical and mental health and create a strong urge to use them again — addiction.

q.t: Who worked out the structure of vitamin B12?
q.e: Dorothy Hodgkin did, and won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1964.

q.t: Why does adolescence exist as a stage at all?
o: The body must mature before it can reproduce
q.e: No living thing can reproduce right after birth — like a seed growing into a mature plant. Adolescence is the preparation period.

q.t: A girl's cycle is 33 days long. Is that healthy?
q.e: The cycle varies between people; anywhere from 21 to 35 days is common and healthy.

q.t: A boy has no Adam's apple at 16. What does this mean?
o: He hasn't reached puberty at all
q.e: Some people never show an Adam's apple; the changes vary and are all normal.

q.t: Which is the scientific view on keeping menstruating girls apart from others?
q.e: Menstruation is a natural, healthy process. Such taboos only cause fear and shame.

q.t: An adolescent girl feels tired and pale. Which deficiency is a likely cause?
q.e: Low iron or B12 can cause anaemia — a blood problem that brings tiredness and paleness.

q.t: Which food would best help someone with iron deficiency?
q.e: Spinach, kidney beans, raisins and figs are good sources of iron.

q.t: Why is understanding mood swings useful?
o: You can pause and choose your response
q.e: Knowing emotions drive behaviour lets you pause and decide, instead of just reacting.

q.t: Which is a positive way to channel strong emotions?
q.e: Creativity and compassion turn strong feelings into strengths.

q.t: Why is peer pressure especially strong in adolescence?
o: It's a stage of curiosity and wanting to fit in
q.e: Curiosity, excitement and the wish to fit in make peers' influence strong. Knowing this in advance makes saying no easier.

q.t: Which online habit is safest?
o: Think before posting and keep personal details private
Share your address with new friends
Use the same password everywhere and share it
q.e: Protecting privacy online keeps you safe from misuse and bullying.

q.t: Regular exercise in adolescence mainly helps by…
q.e: Exercise keeps both the body and mind fit.

q.t: Which of these is NOT a secondary sexual characteristic?
q.e: Height increases from birth in everyone; it doesn't distinguish males from females. The others do.

q.t: Acne is the ___; pimples are ___.
q.e: Acne is the skin condition; pimples are the visible spots it causes.

q.t: Why is a balanced diet most important during adolescence?
o: Rapid growth needs fuel and building material
q.e: Growth is fastest in adolescence, so the body needs proteins, calcium, iron and energy.

q.t: Which pair matches the nutrient to its job correctly?
q.e: Calcium builds bones; iron is for blood; protein is for growth and strength.

q.t: Which is a government scheme for menstrual hygiene?
q.e: MHS, RKSK, Suvidha and state schemes like Shuchi support adolescent health and hygiene.

q.t: A friend posts a false rumour about a classmate online. This is…
q.e: Spreading false rumours online to harass someone is cyberbullying.

q.t: Why are biodegradable pads recommended?
o: They break down naturally and are eco-friendly
q.e: Biodegradable materials decompose naturally, so they don't pile up as waste.

q.t: Which describes what happens to growth in height over a life?
o: Continuous from birth, fastest in adolescence
q.e: Growth is continuous from birth but most rapid in adolescence.

q.t: Stages of life in order:
o: Infancy → childhood → adolescence → adulthood → old age
Childhood → infancy → adulthood → adolescence → old age
Adolescence → infancy → childhood → adulthood → old age
Infancy → adolescence → childhood → old age → adulthood
q.e: Infancy comes first, then childhood, adolescence, adulthood and finally old age.

q.t: Someone offers you gutka 'just to try once'. The best scientific reason to refuse:
o: It is addictive — trying once can start regular use
It is only bad for adults
q.e: Addiction creates a strong urge to repeat, leading to substance abuse that damages health.
